dedupe_keys.name: stram strategic network design model for national freight transport decarbonisation norway

description: STraM is a strategic network design model for decarbonising national freight transport, presented in an arXiv preprint (first version April 2023, revised August 2024) and published in Transportation Research Part E in 2025. The authors argue that national freight models, although used to assess policies and investments against decarbonisation targets, struggle with the development and adoption of new fuel technologies over time, inertia in transport fleets and uncertainty about future transport costs. STraM includes these factors explicitly and returns a network design plan of infrastructure investments and fuel technology decisions for cost-effective decarbonisation of the freight system. Its output can feed higher-resolution national freight transport models for more operational detail. The model is demonstrated in a case study of Norway. Coverage: Norwegian national freight network. Access: open preprint and journal article. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: the abstract does not name a code release or data set, and the model is strategic, so operational disruption is outside its scope. It supports optimisation and capacity planning of multimodal freight networks under long-term uncertainty. It relates to the TRUST European transport model and the ETISplus-based freight flow data in the catalogue.
